name: Tubal-cain
overview: Tubal-cain is a male figure noted in Scripture as the forger of all implements of bronze and iron. His unique role highlights an early development in metalworking technology. There are no specific tribal affiliations or additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Tubal-cain appears only once in Genesis 4:22 and does not have a specified meaning provided in the text. It is a proper name given without indication that it was divinely assigned.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture infers that Tubal-cain is the son of Lamech and Zillah, and he has a sister named Naamah. These relationships are noted in Genesis 4:22 and provide a familial context for his identity.
scriptureSignificance: Tubal-cain's significance lies in his pioneering role as the craftsman of bronze and iron tools, marking a notable advancement in human industry and craftsmanship. This contribution situates him as a key figure in the early development of civilization as recorded in the Bible. His mention alongside his family underscores the biblical emphasis on lineage and the spread of skills through generations.
